findings.description: This bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block and no KMS key, so encryption at rest is not enforced by configuration; sensitive content such as the vendor roster surfaced by aws_s3_bucket_object.reports_seed_object (vendor-roster.xlsx) is left relying on the account/bucket default rather than an explicit, auditable SSE-KMS configuration.

The ledger-exports bucket has acl = "private" but no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving financial ledger exports stored without a configured encryption-at-rest control or customer-managed key.
Versioning and access logging are configured, but the bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored without explicitly enforced encryption at rest.

The runbooks bucket has versioning enabled and acl = "private" but no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational documentation that frequently contains internal hostnames, endpoints and procedures is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
